sources.entry: Ueli - A keystroke launcher for macOS (and Windows) like Spotlight or Alfred.

summary.one_liner: Ueli is a cross-platform keystroke launcher for Windows, macOS and Linux that searches apps, files, web and system items, with extensible modules.
summary.what_it_does: Ueli opens a search window via a global hotkey (Alt+Space by default) where you type to find and launch items. Results can be acted on through an additional-actions menu (Cmd+K on macOS, Ctrl+K elsewhere), and frequently used items can be pinned to favorites. Settings are opened from the app, where extensions can be enabled or disabled and configured individually. The README lists 23 extensions, including Application Search, File Search, Browser Bookmarks, Calculator, Currency Conversion, Web Search, Password Generator, Terminal Launcher, Visual Studio Code and JetBrains Toolbox. A Debug section in settings shows logs for troubleshooting. The README also includes developer setup using Node.js 24 with npm scripts for dev, lint, typecheck, tests, build and packaging.
use_cases: launch apps quickly from the keyboard
do quick calculations and currency conversions
run web searches from a launcher
open projects in Visual Studio Code or JetBrains Toolbox
how_to_run: Windows: winget install Ueli -s msstore (or download from the Microsoft Store or the project website/repository)
macOS and Linux: download and install the app from the project website or repository releases
stack: Electron-style desktop app (inferred from packaging scripts; not named in README, so treat as unconfirmed)
notable: Cross-platform keystroke launcher with a Spotlight/Alfred-style workflow
Modular extensions that can be toggled on or off individually
Favorites that always appear first in search results
Built-in Debug log view in settings for troubleshooting
Available through the Microsoft Store and winget on Windows
caveats: macOS and Windows binaries from direct download are not signed or notarized, so the OS may block installation until manually allowed
Global hotkeys may not work under Linux Wayland sessions; a workaround via custom shortcuts is documented
Settings section is marked as under construction
